column1: # docs/release/zap-rules.tsv: the ZAP baseline scan's warnings this project has decided about.
# A warning blocks the release unless its rule is here. Columns, separated by tabs:
#   rule id    action (IGNORE, WARN, FAIL, INFO)    rule name    why
# IGNORE needs a real reason: this file is the answer to "why did you accept that?"

column4: responses are deliberately not cached: they're per-user and change every request
only /assets/* is storable, and deliberately: its names carry a content hash, so a year of caching is safe and costs the tenant nothing. Every page, JSON body and 404 is no-store
the app is a React single-page app (ADR-0010); this rule only says the scanner can't follow links a script draws

require-corp would block the tenant's own photos, which are served from S3 by pre-signed URL and carry no CORP header. The app sets Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy to same-origin, and a content security policy of 'self'

the five numbers are SHA-256 round constants, not times: @aws-crypto/sha256-js (constants.ts, pulled in by aws-amplify for Cognito sign-in) writes them as hex and esbuild emits them as decimal, so 0x71374491 reaches the bundle as 1899447441. The rule flags any ten-digit integer; nothing here discloses a time
